angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,365,380 km at 30.97 pc = 1.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 109268: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 32.29 +/- 0.21 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1134/S1063773712050015): 30.969 +/- 0.201 pc; Gaia DR3 gives this source no parallax (a two-parameter solution)
radiusSource: Radius 3.4 +/- 0.23 solar radii from Computed here, not printed by a paper: 3.4 +/- 0.23 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.02 +/- 0.07 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 32.29 +/- 0.21 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/167.1.121): 2,365,380 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 14050 +/- 540 K from Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 209952: effective temperature 14050 +/- 540 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 209952: effective temperature 14050 +/- 540 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf Gru: spectral type B6V (2006AJ....132..161G)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf Gru: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * alf Gru: projected rotation speed 215 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)
